              title: Initials

                first and last names, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string

              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-

                global 4-digit zero-padded sequence equal to one more than the number
                of owners at the time this owner was created.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007'
              readOnly: true

              readOnly: true

                owner is created with 'sharesHousehold' true and their lastName and
                address already belong to an existing owner (compared case-insensitively
                with collapsed whitespace), the joiner and the existing household members
                are all assigned this same identifier. It is absent for an owner that does
                not share a household with anyone.
              type: string
              example: 'A1B2C3D4E5F6'
              readOnly: true

                created, sharing this owner's firstName and lastName (compared
                case-insensitively). It is zero when no earlier owner shared both names.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true

          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to
            E.164 form: an explicit leading '+' and country code are kept, otherwise
            country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the
            national digits; spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped. The result must
            be a '+' followed by 8 to 15 digits, and this E.164 value is stored and
            returned.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when supplied it must be a
            syntactically valid address and is normalized to lower case before being
            stored and returned.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The 4-digit postcode of the pet owner. Optional; validated only when
            supplied. When present it must be valid for the owner's city per a fixed
            table keyed by the city's region (Sydney -> NSW 2000-2099, Melbourne ->
            VIC 3000-3099, Brisbane -> QLD 4000-4099); a city with no known region
            accepts any 4-digit postcode. An out-of-range postcode is rejected with
            400. The stored value is returned on read.
          type: string
          pattern: "^[0-9]{4}$"
          example: '2000'

          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current
            date. The stored value is returned on read.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2013-01-01'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The date of birth of the pet owner, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            Optional; when supplied it is stored and returned, and drives the
            derived ageBand.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'

          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Create-only flag acknowledging that this owner deliberately shares a
            household with an existing owner. When omitted or false, a create whose
            lastName and address already belong to another owner (compared
            case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace) is rejected with 409;
            when true the create is allowed to proceed. The flag is not persisted.
          type: boolean
          example: false

            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: >-

              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: >-
                The owner's initials: the upper-cased first letters of the stored
                first and last names, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code, formatted '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where LAST3 is
                the upper-cased first three letters of the last name and NNNN is a
                global 4-digit zero-padded sequence equal to one more than the number
                of owners at the time this owner was created.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007'
              readOnly: true
            checkDigit:
              title: Check digit
              description: >-
                The Luhn check digit (0-9) computed over the digits contained in the
                owner's customerCode.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              maximum: 9
              example: 8
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                A stable identifier shared by the owners of a single household. When an
                owner is created with 'sharesHousehold' true and their lastName and
                address already belong to an existing owner (compared case-insensitively
                with collapsed whitespace), the joiner and the existing household members
                are all assigned this same identifier. It is absent for an owner that does
                not share a household with anyone.
              type: string
              example: 'A1B2C3D4E5F6'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                The number of owners who already existed, at the time this owner was
                created, sharing this owner's firstName and lastName (compared
                case-insensitively). It is zero when no earlier owner shared both names.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: >-
                The owner's membership number, formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>' where
                customerCode is the owner's customer code and YY is the last two digits
                of the registrationDate year.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007-M26'
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: >-
                The owner's membership level, a number from 1 to 3 fixed at creation. It
                starts at 1, gains a level when an email address is present, and gains a
                level when the owner has no namesakes (namesakeCount is zero), capped at 3.
                Level 4 is reserved for tenure.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 3
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: >-
                The owner's locality (region) derived from the stored city using a fixed
                city-to-region table (Sydney -> NSW, Melbourne -> VIC, Brisbane -> QLD).
                It is 'UNKNOWN' for any city not in the table.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true
            bulkSignupWarning:
              title: Bulk signup warning
              description: >-
                True when more than 80 owners have already been created for today's
                registration date at the time of this response, signalling that the
                daily create volume is approaching the per-day limit; otherwise false.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            ageBand:
              title: Age band
              description: >-
                The owner's age band derived from birthDate computed against the
                registrationDate: 'MINOR' when under 18, 'ADULT' from 18 to 64,
                and 'SENIOR' at 65 or older. Absent when no birthDate is present.
              type: string
              example: 'ADULT'
              readOnly: true
            contactPreference:
              title: Contact preference
              description: >-
                The owner's preferred contact channel, derived from the stored
                fields: 'EMAIL' when an email address is present, otherwise 'PHONE'.
              type: string
              example: 'EMAIL'
              readOnly: true
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: >-
                The single derived value used to detect duplicate owners: the owner's
                normalized telephone, email (empty when none) and householdId (empty
                when none) joined by '|'. Two owners are duplicates only when their whole
                identity key is identical, so members of one household with different
                telephones have different keys and are both allowed.
              type: string
              example: '+61412345678|owner@example.test|A1B2C3D4E5F6'
              readOnly: true
          required:

## Summary

Implemented the soft-match ("possible duplicate") rule for owner creation. When a new owner isn't a hard duplicate but shares an existing owner's `lastName` and `postcode` with a different telephone, it's still created and flagged.

**Changes:**

1. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — after the existing hard-duplicate identity check, added `applyPossibleDuplicate(owner)`. The new method finds the lowest-id existing owner whose normalized last name and postcode match the new owner's but whose telephone differs; if found it sets `possibleDuplicate=true` and `possibleDuplicateOf=<matching id>`, otherwise `possibleDuplicate=false`. Last-name comparison reuses the existing `normalizeHouseholdField` (case-insensitive, whitespace-collapsed) for consistency with the other rules.

2. **`Owner` model** — added two persistent fields `possibleDuplicate` (`Boolean`, `possible_duplicate`) and `possibleDuplicateOf` (`Integer`, `possible_duplicate_of`) with getters/setters, so the flags survive a later `GET /api/owners/{id}`.

3. **`openapi.yml`** — added the two read-only properties to the `Owner` schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` carries them and MapStruct maps them by name automatically.

4. **Schema SQL** (hsqldb, h2, mysql, postgres) — added the two new columns to the `owners` table, and appended the two `NULL` values to the positional seed inserts in `hsqldb/data.sql` (the only data file using positional inserts; the others use explicit column lists).

I persisted the flags to the database rather than computing them transiently, since `GET` returns them as values fixed at creation, which requires them to outlive the create request in a real deployment.
